title: Kathmandu vs Paro: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: Choose Kathmandu for a vibrant, budget-friendly dive into ancient history and bustling markets, ideal for backpackers and culture vultures with a daily budget of $30-60 USD. Opt for Paro if you seek tranquility, pristine nature, and a deeply preserved culture with a luxury-leaning budget of $200-300

categories.name: h2 id="culture-history">🏛️ Culture & History
categories.summary: Kathmandu offers a richer, more diverse, and more accessible array of ancient cultural and historical sites.

categories.name: h2 id="costs-budget">💰 Costs & Budget
categories.summary: Kathmandu offers significantly lower daily costs, allowing for extensive travel on a tight budget, unlike Paro's mandatory high daily tariff.

categories.name: h2 id="getting-there-around">✈️ Getting There & Around
categories.summary: Kathmandu is easier and cheaper to reach with more flight options, and offers diverse, affordable local transport for independent exploration.

categories.name: h2 id="nature-scenery">⛰️ Nature & Scenery
categories.summary: Paro boasts unparalleled pristine Himalayan landscapes, clean air, and deeply integrated natural beauty, largely untouched by urban development.

categories.name: h2 id="accommodation">🏨 Accommodation
categories.summary: Kathmandu wins for choice and budget flexibility, while Paro wins for guaranteed quality and curated experience within its package. It's a tie based on different value propositions.

categories.name: h2 id="food-drink">🍜 Food & Drink
categories.summary: Kathmandu offers a vastly more diverse, accessible, and affordable culinary scene, with abundant street food and international options.

categories.name: h2 id="safety-vibe">🛡️ Safety & Vibe
categories.summary: Paro offers an exceptionally safe, serene, and peaceful environment with virtually no crime, providing a stark contrast to Kathmandu's bustling chaos.

categories.name: h2 id="day-trips-activities">🗺️ Day Trips & Activities
categories.summary: Kathmandu provides a much wider and more diverse range of accessible day trips, from historical cities to nature hikes and trekking starting points.

categories.name: h2 id="shopping-souvenirs">🛍️ Shopping & Souvenirs
categories.summary: Kathmandu offers a significantly wider variety of goods, more vibrant market experiences, and better prices for souvenirs, with bargaining expected.

categories.name: h2 id="unique-experience-exclusivity">🌟 Unique Experience/Exclusivity
categories.summary: Paro provides a uniquely exclusive, pristine, and tranquil experience shaped by Bhutan's 'Gross National Happiness' philosophy and controlled tourism.

faq.question: What are the visa requirements for Kathmandu vs Paro?
faq.answer: For Nepal (Kathmandu), most nationalities can obtain a visa on arrival at Tribhuvan Airport (KTM) or land borders. A 30-day tourist visa typically costs around $50 USD. For Bhutan (Paro), a visa is mandatory and is processed by your licensed Bhutanese tour operator as part of your Minimum Daily Package. You cannot apply for a Bhutanese visa independently.

faq.question: When is the best time to visit Kathmandu and Paro?
faq.answer: The best time for both destinations is during the autumn (September to November) for clear skies, moderate temperatures, and festive seasons, and spring (March to May) for rhododendron blooms and pleasant weather. Winter (December to February) can be cold but clear, while monsoon season (June to August) brings heavy rains and leeches, though the landscapes are lush.

faq.question: Are these destinations suitable for solo travelers?
faq.answer: Kathmandu is excellent for solo travelers, with a vibrant hostel scene, easy access to tours and treks, and many opportunities to meet other travelers. Paro is also safe for solo travelers, but the experience is highly structured through guided tours, which means less spontaneous solo exploration but enhanced safety and convenience. Both are generally very welcoming.

faq.question: Can I combine a trip to Kathmandu and Paro?
faq.answer: Absolutely! Combining Kathmandu and Paro is a popular and rewarding way to experience both the vibrant chaos of Nepal and the serene exclusivity of Bhutan. Drukair and Bhutan Airlines operate direct flights between Kathmandu (KTM) and Paro (PBH), taking about 1 hour. This makes for an easy transition, typically requiring 7-10 days in Nepal and 5-7 days in Bhutan for a comprehensive trip.

faq.question: What is the internet and mobile connectivity like?
faq.answer: In Kathmandu, Wi-Fi is widely available in hotels, cafes, and restaurants, though speeds can be inconsistent. Local SIM cards (Ncell, Nepal Telecom) are cheap and offer decent 4G coverage. In Paro, most hotels offer Wi-Fi, often included in your package, but it might be slower than you're used to. Mobile coverage is good in towns but spotty in remote areas. A local Bhutanese SIM can be purchased, but your guide will often facilitate communication.

faq.question: How should I prepare for altitude sickness?
faq.answer: While Kathmandu (1,400m / 4,600ft) and Paro (2,200m / 7,200ft) are not extremely high, some day trips or treks from Kathmandu (e.g., to Everest Base Camp) or hikes in Bhutan (e.g., to Tiger's Nest) reach higher altitudes. It's advisable to stay hydrated, avoid alcohol and strenuous activity on your first day, and ascend gradually if planning higher treks. Consult your doctor for medication like Diamox if you're concerned.

faq.question: What currency should I use in each destination?
faq.answer: In Nepal (Kathmandu), the local currency is the Nepalese Rupee (NPR). ATMs are plentiful, and major credit cards are accepted in larger establishments. USD is accepted by some tourist businesses but it's best to pay in NPR. In Bhutan (Paro), the local currency is the Bhutanese Ngultrum (BTN), which is pegged to the Indian Rupee (INR). Both BTN and INR are accepted. ATMs are available, and credit cards are accepted in major hotels and stores. Your tour package costs are typically paid in USD before arrival.

faq.question: Is it ethical to visit Bhutan given the Minimum Daily Package?
faq.answer: Bhutan's Minimum Daily Package (MDP) is specifically designed to support its 'High Value, Low Impact' tourism policy, which funds free education, healthcare, and infrastructure, and helps preserve its unique culture and pristine environment. Many travelers consider this a highly ethical model as it directly benefits the local population and prevents mass tourism. Your visit contributes to sustainable development, rather than just profit.
